faq.q: Is Class 9 the only choice after Class 8?
faq.a: Most students go to Class 9 and sit SEE in Class 10. A technical stream inside school and short CTEVT skill training are the other doors. The skill route is useful if you want to earn early or learn a trade, and you can still return to formal study later.

faq.q: Which subjects matter most in Class 9 and 10?
faq.a: Maths, Science and English open the most doors after SEE. Weak Maths narrows the science and engineering paths, while strong English helps in management, media, hotel and every study abroad route.

faq.q: Which stream should I take after SEE?
faq.a: Pick the work you can see yourself doing at 25, then work backwards. Science leads to engineering, medicine, IT and nursing. Management leads to business, banking and finance. Humanities and Education lead to law, media, social work and teaching. A stream decides your first degree options, not your whole life.

faq.q: Is a CTEVT diploma a good alternative to +2?
faq.a: Yes, if you want a job-ready skill in three years: engineering, health, agriculture or hospitality. Ask the college and the university whether the diploma is accepted for the bachelor programme you may want later, because acceptance depends on the programme.

faq.q: What about A Levels instead of NEB +2?
faq.a: A Levels follow the Cambridge system and cost more. They suit students planning to study abroad and who are comfortable with English. NEB +2 is cheaper and leads straight into Nepali entrance exams and universities.

faq.q: Can I join the police or army after SEE?
faq.a: Some entry levels in Nepal Police, Armed Police Force and Nepal Army accept SEE passed candidates, with a fitness and written test. Higher posts need +2 or a bachelor. Check the current vacancy notice for age and height limits.

faq.q: I studied Science. What are my options?
faq.a: Science opens the widest set: engineering, medicine and dental, nursing, pharmacy, IT, laboratory and public health, agriculture, architecture, plus management and humanities too. Entrance exams decide medicine and engineering, so start preparing during Class 12.

faq.q: I studied Management. What now?
faq.a: BBS, BBA, BHM, BTTM and BCA are the common choices. BBA and BCA programmes usually ask for an entrance test and a higher cost, BBS is the most affordable. Add a practical skill such as accounting software, data or communication alongside the degree.

faq.q: Is Humanities a weak stream?
faq.a: No. Law, journalism, social work, education, public administration and civil service preparation all start here. The degree matters less than the skills you build: writing, research, speaking and a second language.

faq.q: How do entrance exams work for medicine and engineering?
faq.a: Seats in government and many private colleges are filled through common entrance exams. Medicine and dental use a national medical entrance. Engineering uses the exam of the university or college. Watch the official notice for dates, and prepare Physics, Chemistry, Maths or Biology from the NEB books.

faq.q: Can a Science student study BBA or Law?
faq.a: Yes. Most bachelor programmes in management, humanities and law accept students of any stream. A few technical programmes ask for specific subjects, so read the entry line on each course.

faq.q: Should I do a master's right away or work first?
faq.a: A master's straight after a bachelor suits research, teaching and fields that need it for licence or pay. Business and IT graduates often gain more from one or two years of work first, then an MBA or MSc with a clear goal.

faq.q: How does the Lok Sewa civil service route work?
faq.a: The Public Service Commission announces vacancies by level and service. A bachelor is the common entry for officer level. The path is a written exam, then interview. Start with the syllabus of the service you want and practise past questions.

faq.q: What licences do professionals need in Nepal?
faq.a: Engineers, doctors, nurses, pharmacists, lawyers and teachers register or pass a licence exam with their council or commission before practising. Plan for it in your last year of study.

faq.q: Is ACCA or CA worth it?
faq.a: For finance and audit careers, yes. They are long, exam-heavy and pay off with steady effort, and many students begin while finishing a bachelor. Compare ACCA, CMA, CFA and CA by the job you want.

faq.q: What do I need to study abroad?
faq.a: An accepted university offer, an English test such as IELTS or PTE for most countries, proof of funds, and a visa. Some countries also ask for GRE, GMAT, SAT or a language certificate. Check each country's current rules, they change.

faq.q: How do I avoid fake consultancies?
faq.a: Never pay a large fee before you have a written offer. Apply directly to universities when you can. Check the consultancy is registered, ask for receipts, and confirm every offer on the university's own website.

faq.q: Which scholarships can Nepali students apply for?
faq.a: Government and embassy scholarships such as Chevening, Commonwealth, Fulbright, DAAD, MEXT, GKS, Australia Awards, Eiffel, SISGP, VLIR-UOS and ADB-JSP open every year, plus university scholarships. Deadlines are fixed, so note them six to nine months early.

faq.q: What is the CTEVT 18-month Pre-Diploma (TSLC) route?
faq.a: Pre-Diploma is an 18-month practical course in civil sub-overseer, electrical, mechanical, computer, JTA agriculture or ANM. It costs very little at public polytechnics, lets you apply for Junior Technical Assistant jobs, and gives lateral entry seats into a 3-year diploma.

faq.q: How do PCL Nursing, HA (General Medicine) and Diploma in Pharmacy compare?
faq.a: All three are 3-year CTEVT clinical courses entered after SEE with at least GPA 2.0 and C grades in Maths, Science and English. PCL Nursing (tuition cap NPR 4.75 lakh) leads to Staff Nurse posts and BNS. HA (cap NPR 4.04 lakh) runs primary health posts and leads to BPH or MBBS. Diploma in Pharmacy (cap NPR 3.38 lakh) trains Pharmacy Assistants and leads to BPharm.

faq.q: How does the Indian Embassy Mahatma Gandhi Scholarship (MGSS) work for Class 11?
faq.a: Regular Class 11 students in Nepal with at least 60% in SEE and family income below NPR 200,000 per year can apply online on goischolarship.com.np in October or November. Selected students receive NPR 24,000 per year for Class 11 and 12 directly in their bank account. Never apply through middlemen or consultancies, as those forms are rejected.

faq.q: What is the difference between BSc CSIT, BCA, BIT and BIM?
faq.a: All four are 4-year IT degrees in Nepal that lead to software, data and product jobs. BSc CSIT requires +2 Science (or Maths) and leans deeper into computer science theory and algorithms. BIT and BCA focus heavily on software, web and mobile projects and accept students from non-science streams too. BIM is under TU Faculty of Management (CMAT entrance) and blends 60% IT with 40% management.

faq.q: What is the difference between an IOE Regular seat and a Full Fee seat?
faq.a: At TU IOE's five constituent campuses (Pulchowk, Thapathali, Purwanchal, Paschimanchal and Chitwan), 630 of the 2,040 bachelor seats are Regular merit seats where 4-year tuition is around NPR 63,000, while Full Fee seats cost around NPR 5.46 lakh for the exact same classes and degree. Private IOE affiliated colleges charge NPR 10 to 20 lakh.

faq.q: How do MECEE-BL medical scholarships and official MEC fee caps work?
faq.a: All bachelor medical and allied health admissions in Nepal go through the 200-mark MECEE-BL exam at entrance.mec.gov.np. Public medical colleges reserve 75% of seats as government scholarships (55% open merit, 45% inclusive categories). For paying seats, MEC fixes tuition caps: MBBS NPR 40.23 lakh inside Kathmandu Valley and 45.96 lakh outside, BDS 20.92 lakh, BAMS 11.32 lakh, BSc Nursing 10.36 lakh, BNS 5.18 lakh, and BPharm, BPH, BMLT, BPT, BOptom and BSc MIT at NPR 7.77 lakh each.

faq.q: Should I study 5-year BA LLB after +2 or 3-year LLB after a bachelor?
faq.a: If you are certain after +2 that you want a legal, judicial or civil service career, the 5-year BA LLB or BBA LLB saves a year and gives intensive moot court and clinic training. If you want a first degree in science, IT, management or humanities first, you can take the 3-year LLB afterward.

faq.q: Which council licence exams are mandatory before working in Nepal?
faq.a: Graduating is only step one in regulated fields. Doctors and dentists must pass the Nepal Medical Council (NMC) exam, engineers register through the Nepal Engineering Council (NEC) exam, nurses pass the Nepal Nursing Council (NNC) exam, pharmacists pass the Nepal Pharmacy Council (NPC) exam, allied health graduates register with the NHPC, and lawyers pass the Nepal Bar Council exam.

faq.q: Can I study MBBS abroad and practise as a doctor in Nepal?
faq.a: Only if you pass Nepal's MECEE-BL entrance (or meet the Medical Education Commission's foreign study eligibility percentile) before going abroad, verify that the foreign medical university and teaching hospital are recognised, complete the required clinical internship, and pass the NMC licensing exam on return.

faq.q: How do EPS Korea and Japan SSW skill routes work safely?
faq.a: South Korea's EPS-TOPIK is run government-to-government through the EPS Nepal office under the Department of Foreign Employment, never through private manpower agents. Japan's Specified Skilled Worker (SSW) route requires passing JLPT N4 or JFT-Basic plus a sector skill test in caregiving, agriculture, food service or construction via Prometric.

faq.q: How do I choose between money and interest?
faq.a: Look at both: demand today, competition, and the pay at entry and senior level, then ask which daily work you would not mind doing for ten years. A career where you improve every year pays better than one you chose only for the first salary.

faq.q: Do I have to decide everything now?
faq.a: No. Choose the next step, keep options open, and build skills that travel across fields: communication, numbers, one digital skill and English. Many people change fields after their first degree.

faq.q: How do I check if a college and degree are genuinely recognised in Nepal?
faq.a: Check three things before paying admission fees: affiliation on the university's official website (TU, KU, PU, PoU, AFU, FWU, MWU, LBU, RJU or CTEVT), equivalence from TU Curriculum Development Centre if it is a foreign degree taught in Nepal, and approval from the relevant professional council (NEC, MEC/NMC, NNC, NPC or NHPC) for technical and health courses.

faq.q: Can I still sit SEE if I dropped out or have to work during the day?
faq.a: Yes. Selected public schools run CEHRD Open and Alternative Secondary School programmes where working youth, mothers and returning learners study flexibly and sit the exact same NEB SEE board examination. You can also take an 18-month CTEVT Pre-Diploma or 390-hour skill training to earn early.

faq.q: What are CMLT, Radiography, Ophthalmic Science and Dental Hygiene under CTEVT?
faq.a: These are 3-year clinical paramedical diplomas after SEE requiring at least GPA 2.0 and C grades in English, Maths and Science. At CTEVT constituent schools like School of Health Science Bharatpur, subsidised seats cost around NPR 52,000 and full-pay seats NPR 1.33 to 3.28 lakh, while private colleges cap between NPR 3.40 and 3.98 lakh. All four qualify for Level 5 health posts after NHPC registration and open bachelor paths in BMLT, BSc MIT, BOptom or BDS.

faq.q: What is Actuarial Science (BMathSc) at Tribhuvan University and why is it in demand?
faq.a: Tribhuvan University's School of Mathematical Sciences in Balkhu runs a 4-year (8-semester) Bachelor in Mathematical Sciences in Actuarial Science and a Bachelor in Data Science. Actuaries use probability, statistics and financial mathematics to price insurance policies and value pension and reinsurance risks. Because Nepal has a shortage of licensed actuaries, insurance companies, banks and analytics teams hire graduates steadily.

faq.q: What is BICTE and how is it different from BEd or BCA?
faq.a: BICTE (Bachelor of Information and Communication Technology Education) is a 4-year semester degree under TU Faculty of Education that combines software programming, databases and networking with teaching pedagogy. Unlike a general BEd it gives strong computing coursework, and unlike BCA it directly satisfies the education requirement for the Teacher Service Commission computer teacher licence.

faq.q: What are BASLP, BPerfusionTech and BMid under the Medical Education Commission?
faq.a: These are specialised 4-year clinical bachelor degrees admitted through MECEE-BL. BASLP trains audiologists and speech-language therapists, BPerfusionTech and BSc Anaesthesia train cardiac bypass and operation-theatre technologists (MEC paying tuition cap NPR 7.77 lakh each), and BMid trains autonomous professional midwives (MEC paying cap NPR 10.36 lakh, with 75% scholarship seats in public academies).

faq.q: How do Nepal Rastra Bank (NRB), public bank and NEA/NTC officer exams work?
faq.a: Public enterprises such as Nepal Rastra Bank, Rastriya Banijya Bank, Nepal Bank, Agricultural Development Bank, Nepal Electricity Authority, Nepal Telecom and CAAN fill permanent officer and assistant posts through competitive written exams conducted by the Public Service Commission. Graduates in Economics, Management, CA, IT, Engineering and Law are the primary eligible groups.

faq.q: How do the Indian Embassy COMPEX, Silver Jubilee (SJSS) and AYUSH scholarships work?
faq.a: The Embassy of India in Kathmandu runs separate annual schemes for studying in India: COMPEX (opening around April-May for BE, BPharm, BSc Agriculture, Dairy/Food Tech and BSc Nursing after +2 Science), AYUSH (May-June for BAMS, BHMS, BUMS and postgraduate traditional medicine via the ICCR A2A portal), Homi Jahangir Bhabha (February-March for ME/MTech), and Silver Jubilee SJSS (February-March for MBA, MCA, MSc, MA and PhD via a2ascholarships.iccr.gov.in). Always apply directly and never through middlemen.

faq.q: What does UGC QAA accreditation mean when choosing a community campus in Nepal?
faq.a: Nepal has more than 540 community-run public campuses offering low-fee TU, PU, FWU and MWU degrees across all 77 districts. Campuses that earn Quality Assurance and Accreditation (QAA) from the University Grants Commission (UGC) have passed an independent peer review of their faculty, library, calendar and exam standards, and also offer UGC need-based and girls scholarships.

faq.q: Can I switch from Science to Management, Law, IT or Arts after +2?
faq.a: Yes. A +2 Science graduate can apply to almost every bachelor stream in Nepal, including BBA, BBS, BIM, BCA, BIT, BMathSc Actuarial Science, 5-year BA LLB, BHM, Economics and Psychology. Moving the other way (from Management or Humanities into Engineering or Medicine) is restricted because NEC and MEC require Physics, Chemistry and Maths or Biology at +2.
